name: Subscription Pricing URL Discovery
description: Finds the subscription pricing page URL for an AI provider by scanning links, classifying pages, and verifying reachability.
systemPrompt: You are a classification assistant. Analyze the provided page content and classify it into exactly one of the allowed answers. Return JSON with 'answer', 'observation' (one short sentence), and optional 'confidence'.
task: Find the subscription pricing page URL for {{providerName}}.

init-state.name: Initialize State
init-state.description: Initializes the verification state from the current research data.

is-self-hosted.name: Is Self-Hosted Provider
is-self-hosted.description: Checks whether the provider is self-hosted (a local application with no subscription plans to price).

record-current-fact.name: Record Current Fact
record-current-fact.description: Records the current field value as a verified fact in the research state.

scan-sibling-links.name: Scan Sibling Links
scan-sibling-links.description: Scans known-good sibling pages (apiPricingUrl, documentationUrl) for <a href> links — these pages often link to the subscription pricing page.

has-sibling-candidates.name: Has Sibling Candidates
has-sibling-candidates.description: Checks whether sibling page scanning produced any candidates.

scan-provider-links.name: Scan Provider Links
scan-provider-links.description: Scans the provider website homepage for candidate URLs as a fallback.

has-candidates.name: Has Candidates
has-candidates.description: Checks whether any candidate URLs remain to be evaluated.

fetch-next-candidate.name: Fetch Next Candidate
fetch-next-candidate.description: Fetches the next candidate URL from the queue for evaluation.

classify-page.name: Classify Page
classify-page.description: Uses the LLM to classify the fetched page content against the field purpose.
classify-page.task: Classify this page for the field purpose: finding the subscription pricing URL for {providerName}. The page CONTENT is the deciding factor; the candidate URL (visible in State as lastFetchedUrl and in Data source) is only a supporting signal. Paths containing /pricing, /plans, /billing, /subscribe, /token-plan suggest a pricing page — this holds EVEN when the pricing segment appears under /docs/ (e.g. /docs/pricing/overview IS a pricing page, not a generic documentation page). Only treat /api-reference/, /models/, /guides/, or /docs/ paths that have NO pricing/plans/billing/subscribe segment as non-pricing. Classify as 'subscription_pricing' only when the page states a recurring price — an amount bound to a period (per month, per year, per seat, billed monthly or annually); classify as 'both' when the same page displays BOTH pay-per-token API pricing AND such a recurring subscription price. Classify as 'no_subscription' when the page is the provider's own pricing or plans page and there is NO subscription: billing is usage-based only — pay-as-you-go, prepaid credits, a percentage platform fee, per-token or per-request prices, 'no minimum spend', 'pay only for what you use' — with no recurring amount anywhere on the page. A tier or plan comparison table does not by itself make a subscription: Free / Pay-as-you-go / Enterprise columns are 'no_subscription' when none of them carries a recurring price. Keep 'api_pricing' for a per-token price list that says nothing either way about whether a subscription product exists. A pure model-description or API-reference page with no subscription tiers is NOT a subscription pricing page even if it mentions pricing or token plans in navigation. Navigation links to other pages do not define what this page IS. A page announcing that a service or product has been retired, deprecated, discontinued, or is no longer available is NOT a pricing page even if its URL path contains /billing/ or /pricing/ — classify it as 'unrelated'. IMPORTANT: The page MUST be hosted on the provider's own domain. A third-party page (different domain) that merely mentions the provider name or its products is NOT the provider's subscription pricing page — classify it as 'unrelated'. In your observation, always begin with the candidate URL (the lastFetchedUrl value from State) so the reader knows which page was classified.

page-confirms-subscription.name: Page Confirms Subscription
page-confirms-subscription.description: Deterministically verifies the classifier's positive subscription answer against the page that was actually fetched. The answer is overridden to not applicable ('-') only when that page positively declares usage-based billing ('pay as you go') AND never mentions the word 'subscription' — the signature of a per-token price list misread as recurring pricing. A page that mentions 'subscription', or declares neither signal, is left to the classifier.

verify-reachable.name: Verify Reachable
verify-reachable.description: Verifies that the candidate URL is reachable via HTTP.

is-reachable.name: Is Reachable
is-reachable.description: Checks whether the last reachability verification succeeded.

candidates-exhausted.name: Candidates Exhausted
candidates-exhausted.description: Checks whether any queued candidate is still untried in this run.

web-search.name: Web Search
web-search.description: Searches the web for relevant URLs as a fallback strategy.

has-search-results.name: Has Search Results
has-search-results.description: Checks whether the web search produced a candidate that is still untried.

win.name: Success
win.description: Terminal node indicating a successful result.

lose.name: Failure
lose.description: Terminal node indicating no result was found.

not-applicable.name: Not Applicable
not-applicable.description: Terminal node indicating the field is not applicable to this provider.
